summary: Monthly projections meeting run by Chris Klevan with closer Andrew Musial and setter Kim Forbes-Sobers; Richard Claessen was on the call travelling and did not speak, and was asked to submit his numbers on the sheet afterwards. Opens with wins, then works Andrew's July spread week by week against his working days, settling at 23 units and $92,000 cash after he pushes for $100,000 and Chris talks him back to something he will actually hit. Kim projects 110 sets and 22 units after revising her first week down. The back half covers operations: recurring-payment visibility and commission tracking, CRM records getting stuck on rescheduled outcomes, a lead assigned to one closer being worked by another, an injured client and whether he will keep paying, and a proposal from an outside vendor to put setters, closers and prospects together in WhatsApp group chats to improve show rates.
notable: Nationality-based disqualification, from the 1-1 the previous day, is now operational and stated as team policy by the manager: "we're DQing people off the calendar, like you've been giving us feedback, we're getting those people off the calendar, you know, to open up more slots for the U.S. leads." The setter reports executing it on the same call — a prospect from Egypt DQ'd, another from Libya being chased.

A client Andrew closed on 1 June was injured on roughly his second workout. The entire discussion that follows is about whether he will continue paying; no incident review, no question about what he was doing or whether he was cleared. Chris closes it with "not something we can control."

The injury-pause policy is confirmed by two people independently and matches what reps are telling prospects on live calls: "they usually will, like, pause the payment and pause the program until he's fully recovered and then continue it from there" (Kim) and "typically that's what you do in that case if somebody's injured, you pause them" (Chris).

Andrew's average cash collected per close is $3,600 against a $6,000 list price — Chris pulls it live from the sheet. Useful denominator context for the improvised payment structures appearing on his calls.

Team funnel model restated: 7 slots a day, 22 working days, 154 slots, 65% show rate, ~100 live calls, 30% close rate, ~30 units. Andrew settles at 23 units and $92,000 for July after initially wanting $100,000.

An outside vendor and a bot named Sophia are referenced as involved in show-rate optimisation: "the people who manage, you know, the bot, the Sophia, right?" What Sophia does and whether prospects know they are talking to it is not established on this call.

CRM hygiene is poor by the team's own account: cancelled prospects vanish from the closer's calendar, records get stuck on rescheduled outcomes, and a lead assigned to Ben was being called by Andrew. Chris's instruction is to update outcomes from memory — "You don't have to like find the recording or anything. You can just update it real quick."
Andrew never received a commission tracker at onboarding and cannot see recurring payments in sales alerts; he only learns about them if a payment fails.

Andrew declines to use his personal WhatsApp for prospect group chats — "it is my tool for connecting with important people" — despite having exchanged WhatsApp numbers with clients he onboarded the day before and describing that practice on live calls as something he always does.
